title: Microsoft Edge: sign in to Edge with a Google account on Windows and macOS
summary: The roadmap facts, default availability and both policy controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. The statement about the Google identity being outside the tenant needs narrowing, and the question about a future Apple sign-in announcement is out of date.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Accounts; Open questions: Apple announcement
claims.claim: The policy documentation covers Apple accounts as well as Google accounts, whereas this roadmap item names Google.
claims.quote: This policy controls whether users can sign in to Microsoft Edge using non-Microsoft accounts, such as Google or Apple accounts.
claims.fix: Remove the Open questions bullet beginning 'The policy page already names Apple accounts'. The cited Stable archive already announces Apple account sign-in in version 157.0.4341.42, November 05, 2026, and identifies NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled as its control: https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnote-archive-stable-channel.

claims.quote: GP name: Restrict which accounts can be used to sign in to Microsoft Edge; GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge

claims.where: controls[1].api
claims.claim: The Windows registry control is RestrictSigninToPattern, a REG_SZ under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge.
claims.quote: Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge; Value name: RestrictSigninToPattern; Value type: REG_SZ

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: RestrictSigninToPattern limits account usernames using a regular-expression pattern.
claims.quote: You can configure this policy to match multiple accounts using a Perl style regular expression for the pattern. If a user tries to sign in to the browser with an account whose username doesn't match this pattern, they're blocked and will get the appropriate error message.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Already signed-in profiles whose usernames do not match are signed out after RestrictSigninToPattern is enabled.
claims.quote: Signed-in profiles with a username that doesn't match this pattern will be signed out after this policy is enabled.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: RestrictSigninToPattern determines which accounts can be used during the Sync opt-in flow.
claims.quote: Determines which accounts can be used to sign in to the Microsoft Edge account that's chosen during the Sync opt-in flow.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence entitlement for Google account sign-in to Edge.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account sign-in license pricing free subscription; browser licensing prerequisites price Google sign-in. Opened policy, Stable archive, Edge for Business and enterprise sync prerequisites; no Google sign-in licence found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The roadmap, Edge release notes and policy documentation name no price, meter or charge for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account sign in sync data storage licensing price NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled; Google account sign-in license pricing free subscription. Read roadmap, policy, feature entries in Stable archive and Edge for Business; no feature price or meter found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions: synchronisation
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented which browser data a Google-signed-in Edge profile synchronises.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account sign in synchronization data stored sync Microsoft servers. Read policy, Stable archive Google entries, enterprise sync and privacy Sync section; searched privacy text for Google and non-Microsoft. No Google-profile sync data description found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions: synchronisation
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the sync service or storage destination for Google-signed-in Edge profiles.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account sign in synchronization data stored sync Microsoft servers. Read privacy Sync section, enterprise sync, policy and Stable archive Google entries; privacy describes Microsoft accounts, enterprise sync describes Entra accounts, not Google-profile storage.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: A user signed in with a Google account has a browser identity outside the tenant.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Google account identity personal account tenant non Microsoft sign in. Read NonMicrosoftAccountSignInEnabled, privacy Sign in and Identity, and Edge for Business; they do not establish the Google-signed-in profile's relationship to the tenant.
claims.fix: Replace 'A user signed in with a Google account has a browser identity outside the tenant' with 'Google account sign-in is a non-Microsoft account sign-in option', supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies/nonmicrosoftaccountsigninenabled. Keep treating the profile as unmanaged explicitly as advice, not a documented tenant-boundary mechanism.
